title: The Guarded Syntax: A Notation for Linear Resource Calculi
description:
We introduce the Guarded Syntax, a written notation for the Care Calculus, a multi-sorted ordered linear logic with coalgebraic generators and guarded recursion, mechanized in Lean 4. The notation has five operators: the knower, the one Cartesian source; the linear wire, which consumes the left and produces the right exactly once; the guard, one interval of delay; the feed, which binds a delayed output back into its own definition (the +1); and the sink, the archive where content is recorded and never read (the -1). Agent definitions are one-line expressions of this grammar; the notation's operators of consumption, delay and feedback answer exactly the calculus's three structural questions, typographically.

The calculus's two linearity laws appear as expressions that fail to type — a cloner and an eraser are unwritable, while the archive is legal, and that difference is load-bearing — with the laws' theorem statements and machine-checked fragment strengths alongside. The correspondence is stated precisely: well-formed expressions translate to derivations and back, with claims carrying proof sketches and term-level anchors to machine-checked theorems; the linear cut is the rewrite rule that splices a pending binder into the hole it closes, resolving the mutual promise of two abstractions each waiting on the other; and the feed is legal exactly when guarded — the form of the side condition that makes self-application cost a context.

Well-formedness is compositional: there is no global correctness criterion, and the two linearity laws are not forbidden moves to be checked after writing but shapes the grammar simply cannot generate — a linear wire has no junction, and a content wire has no bare end. Every expression in the paper is drawn from a named, machine-checked derivation; the notation-level correspondence is stated, not mechanized.
notes: Deposit license is AGPL-3.0-or-later (see LICENSE), covering the paper's LaTeX source (paper.tex), its macros (guarded-syntax.sty), the compiled paper (paper.pdf), and the gate scripts (scripts/) — matching the paper's own Artifact availability paragraph. The paper carries no figures or drawings: the notation is written, and the gate enforces that. The companion Lean 4 mechanization (Dcare) that the paper's anchors refer to is developed separately and is not part of this deposit; scripts/sync-check.sh is how the paper's anchors are checked against a checkout of it. Two of the paper's 20 anchors, Dcare.no_vanishing_fix_conditional and Dcare.no_vanishing_fixfree_conditional (both in Dcare/Chase.lean), postdate the Chase.lean in the public coglib checkout and are therefore unverified against it.
